correctness.rationale: An exhaustive source-map enumeration and a separate incremental-arc enumeration agree on all 6497 faces for each graph. Both opposite-order discrete-Morse matchings pass complete 29160-incidence acyclicity verification. Integer gradient-path projections yield Wagner critical ranks 15,52,32,10 and a primitive degree-four boundary of rank 11, all other Morse differentials zero; cube critical ranks 8,51,40,12 and primitive boundaries of ranks 2 and 4. Exact row and column unimodular reductions reach only unit diagonal entries and zero residual blocks, proving the integral homology and torsion-freeness. Full simplicial boundary ranks independently computed over two prime fields agree. The included checker and certificate reproduce these facts.

originality.rationale: Three relevant primary preprints were materially inspected. Their cycle/path, tournament, directed-acyclic matching-comparison and bounded-torsion results do not calculate the bidirected Wagner graph. The closest indexed named-Wagner results refer to ordinary matching, Morse or cut complexes. The cube calculation is a known comparator and the top Hamiltonian contribution is not claimed new; the new content is the complete Wagner lower-degree integral calculation and exact face-vector equality with inequivalent homology. Residual risk of a missing equivalent paper remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature or a hidden exact table may calculate the same restricted cycle-free rook-board complex.
The theorem provides integral homology and face-vector equality, not a homotopy equivalence classification or an equivariant representation.

value.rationale: The Wagner M8 and Q3 are canonical, nonisomorphic cubic graphs on the same eight vertices. Their fully bidirected multipath complexes have the same complete face vector but different integral homology in every nonzero degree, an explicit structural warning that the multipath counting polynomial fails to determine homology even in a natural low-order class. The Wagner ranks give a reusable integral benchmark for directed graph topology beyond the path/polygon cases. The invariant is complete for this named object and its comparison is mathematically motivated; no infinite-family theorem is implied.
